verdict: Genuine Parts grew sales 4% to $6.5B, led by its Industrial business at +6%, but net income slipped to $224M as restructuring costs for the planned split of the company into two continued.

segments.name: Automotive — North America
segments.note: NAPA Auto Parts stores and distribution in the U.S. and Canada (segment detail from the company's 10-Q) — comparable sales rose 1.7%.

segments.name: Industrial (Motion)
segments.note: Motion — bearings, power transmission and industrial parts and services (segment detail from the company's 10-Q) — comparable sales rose 5.5%.

segments.name: Automotive — International
segments.note: Auto-parts businesses in Europe and Australasia (segment detail from the company's 10-Q).

opex.name: Selling, administrative & other
opex.note: The cost of running thousands of stores, branches and distribution centers.

opex.name: Restructuring & other costs
opex.note: Restructuring and other costs, including work tied to the planned split of the company.

opex.name: Provision for doubtful accounts
opex.note: Reserves for customer accounts that may not pay.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $46.0M, plus $3.9M of other non-operating expense.
footerNote: Genuine Parts does not print an operating-income line in its release; operating income here ($328.5M) is gross profit less total operating expenses, exactly as its statement foots to pre-tax income. The company announced in February 2026 that it will split into two public companies — Global Automotive and Global Industrial — targeted for the first quarter of 2027.

takeaways.title: Industrial is outgrowing Auto
takeaways.text: Industrial (Motion) sales rose 6.1% to $2.41B on 5.5% comparable growth, while total Automotive sales rose about 3% to $4.11B — North America +2.2%, International +4.5%.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS vs $1.62 GAAP
takeaways.text: Excluding $61M of after-tax adjustments ($0.45 a share) — restructuring and split-related costs — adjusted EPS was $2.07 and adjusted net income about $285M.

takeaways.title: A split is coming
takeaways.text: Genuine Parts is separating into Global Automotive and Global Industrial, targeted for Q1 2027 — the restructuring line ($64.5M this quarter) is the visible cost of becoming two companies.

oneTimers: Restructuring and other costs were $64.5M in the quarter; total after-tax adjustments excluded from adjusted earnings were $61M ($0.45 per share).
